Optimal.Notes: Setting the refresh rate to 40 Hz and matching the frame cap eliminates tearing and gives a smooth, consistent feel; FSR upscaling from 1024x640 recovers image quality lost at reduced resolution. Shadows and AO are the biggest GPU cost — keeping them low frees headroom for stable 40 fps.

profiles.Summary: Star Wars Jedi: Fallen Order runs on the Steam Deck with a gold ProtonDB rating, meaning most players get it working well with minor tweaks. The game is demanding for the Deck's hardware — sitting between minimum and recommended PC specs — so medium-to-low settings with a 40 fps target are the sweet spot for most play sessions.
profiles.BasisNote: No specific Steam Deck player reports were available; profiles are estimated from the PC minimum/recommended requirements versus Deck hardware capability (roughly GTX 1050 Ti class). On your first run, check frame rate during the Zeffo tomb and Kashyyyk jungle sections — the busiest areas — and drop to the Max Battery profile if frame rate dips below 28 fps consistently.

MaxBattery.Notes: Render at 960x600 and use Deck FSR to upscale to 1280x800; the 8 W TDP and GPU clock cap keep temperatures and draw low. Shader pre-compilation stutters will still occur on first run regardless of settings.

KnownIssues: Some players report stuttering during traversal and scene transitions, likely due to shader compilation on first run.
The game may require Proton Experimental or a recent GE-Proton build to launch reliably.
Occasional graphical glitches or crashes have been reported on certain Proton versions.
Loading times can be lengthy on slower storage media.

MaxPerformance.Notes: At full TDP and native resolution the Deck can push into the 50s fps in simpler areas but will dip to the low 40s in dense environments and during combat — expect an uncapped, variable experience rather than a locked 60. Battery life will be short; this profile suits docked or plugged-in play.

Optimal.Notes: The 40 Hz refresh lock paired with a 40 fps cap gives smooth, tear-free gameplay that feels noticeably better than 30 fps; FSR at 1024x640 recovers enough GPU headroom to hold the target in most areas.

profiles.Summary: Star Wars Jedi: Fallen Order is a demanding Unreal Engine 4 action-adventure that sits above the Steam Deck's GPU class at recommended settings, but runs playably at medium-low settings with FSR upscaling. The game holds around 30–40 fps in most areas, though busy combat and open environments can cause dips that require TDP and resolution tuning to manage.
profiles.BasisNote: No Deck-specific player reports were available; profiles are estimated from PC minimum/recommended requirements vs. Deck GPU capability (roughly GTX 1050 Ti class) and general UE4 game behaviour on the Deck. On first run, check frame pacing in the first open outdoor area on Bogano and drop to Max Battery settings if the Optimal profile dips below 35 fps.

MaxBattery.Notes: Rendering at 960x600 with Deck FSR upscaling keeps GPU load low enough to stay near 30 fps on the 8 W TDP budget; motion blur is disabled to reduce perceived choppiness at 30 fps.

KnownIssues: Some areas with dense foliage or large open environments cause notable frame dips below 30 fps even at low settings.
The game is rated Playable (not Verified), with minor UI or launcher quirks reported under Proton.
Shader compilation stutters can occur on first-time area loads.
No native Linux build; runs via Proton with gold-tier compatibility — occasional crashes have been reported by some users.

MaxPerformance.Notes: Full TDP and max GPU clock can push 50–60 fps in corridors and lighter scenes, but expect dips into the 40s in dense outdoor areas; drop Shadow Quality to Low if stutters persist.
